newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures slightly up on JGBs' rise.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures slightly up on JGBs' rise.

text.p: Key December Euroyen deposit rate futures ended Wednesday's TIFFE day session just slightly higher in thin trade.
The December settled at 99.20, after trading between 99.19 and 99.21. Turnover was 13,368 contracts.
"Euroyen futures were a bit firmer due to a rise in Japanese government bonds (JGBs)," said a brokerage house trader.
Key June JGB futures ended up 0.22 at 125.75. The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.300 percent as of 3.40 p.m. (0640 GMT), after falling to a record low of 2.290 percent earlier.
Traders said Euroyen futures' upside was heavy compared with JGB futures.
"Selling pressure seems to intensify above 99.20 for the December contract," said the brokerage house trader.
Traders said some players were starting to say that the negative impact of the planned consumption tax hike might not be as strong as previously thought.
"Due to such a view, it is becoming difficult to chase the price higher," the brokerage house trader said.
Japan will raise the consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1.
The market will be focusing on Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) data for the October-December period due at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT) on Thursday.
Economists polled by Reuters said on average they expect real GDP to grow 0.8 percent quarter-on-quarter. The GDP grew 0.1 percent quarter-on-quarter in the previous quarter.
GDP forecasts ranged from 0.3 to 1.2 percent growth.
Key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.53 percent, up from Tuesday's weighted average of 0.50 percent.
The BOJ injected 400 billion yen into the money market on Wednesday morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
The overnight rate rose due to fund demand ahead of the end of the current reserve maintenance period on Friday, money traders said.
No new certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued so far on Wednesday. Three-month and two-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent. One-month CDs were offered at 0.55 percent.
